reader.requirement: When a USE procedure (the whole remainder of its declarative section) finishes, control must return to the next executable statement after the relative-file I-O statement that caused it, wherever that statement sits (same sentence, an IF branch, nested IF, a performed paragraph's last statement); after a critical status the action is the implementor's, which WiseOwl COBOL documents as continuing with the next executable statement (docs/conformance/3.5).

edition-consulted.switches: EC-free group: ctx.Data.DialectLevel >= 2002 adds the SORT GR17 return-signal exit filter; at 85 the bare try { dispatch } finally { clear active flag } form; both fall through to the statement after the hook
ecState.Active (EC model, reachable only through 2002+ constructs) chooses the DispatchResult-returning invoker; at 85 the void form

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|Edition over DispatchEmitter.cs, EmitterState.cs, SequentialIoEmitter.cs (EmitUseHook) and CobolFile.cs: only the two DispatchEmitter arms above; neither changes where control returns.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb367_use_procedure_is_the_section_85 covers a sequential file's AT END status 10 returning to the statement after a READ; relative-file invalid key, critical statuses (35, 41, 42), returns into IF branches and performed paragraphs are not exercised

probes.printed: A1 after dup WRITE ST=22; USE INPUT MODE then A2 after OPEN missing (35, critical, no FILE STATUS); A3 same sentence ST=23 (READ, no INVALID KEY); A4 in IF after REWRITE ST=23 then A4 after IF; A5 after PERFORM (DELETE last in P-READ, P-NEXT not run); A6 after OPEN open ST=41; A7 after inner IF ST=23 (START in nested IF); A8 after CLOSE closed ST=42; USE ran its PERFORM and GO TO inside the section each time; END CNT=07
probes.expected: after each USE procedure control resumes at the next executable statement after the failing statement; critical statuses continue per the documented implementor choice

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR6  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR6

reader.notes: The I-O statement's hook calls __RunUse and then falls through, so control lands on the next emitted statement in whatever construct holds the I-O statement; abnormal termination is emitted only when no USE procedure ran and the file has no FILE STATUS. The 85 arm of EmitRunUseBody differs from 2002+ only by the SORT GR17 filter. Probe output is identical at --std 85 and 2023.
reader.at-2023: u6a at --std 2023 prints the same lines

refuter.evidence: Attacked the return point where it could go wrong: a READ / REWRITE carrying only NOT INVALID KEY (the NOT phrase must not run after the USE procedure), a DELETE inside an inline PERFORM UNTIL (each iteration must continue), a READ NEXT at end with only NOT AT END, a WRITE duplicate (22), a USE section of two paragraphs left by GO TO to its last paragraph, and a second declarative section that must not be fallen into. rf6a.cob at --std 85: 'D1-Z ST=23 CNT=01 / B1 AFTER ST=23', 'D1-Z ST=23 CNT=02 / B2 SAME-SENTENCE ST=23', 'B3 ITER 1..3' each after its D1-Z, 'D1-A NON23 ST=10 / D1-Z ST=10 / B4 AFTER ST=10', 'D1-A NON23 ST=22 / D1-Z ST=22 / B5 AFTER ST=22', 'D2 RAN ST=35 / B6 AFTER OPEN ST=35 CNT=07' (D1 did not run for Q-FILE). No WRONG line printed; control always resumed at the next executable statement. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR6  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR6'.
